Place various traps on the path to damage and stun enemies!|Store Description}} }} ==Description== The '''Trapper''' is an intermediate [[Towers|tower]] that can be bought for {{Coins|3,000}}. It places down various traps on the ground, which when they come in contact with an enemy, the traps damage it in various ways or apply debuffs to them. All traps can damage [[Hidden (Attribute)|Hidden]] enemies, damage [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemies and bypass defense. When there are no enemies in range, the '''Trapper''' will lay its traps randomly, but if there is an enemy within range the '''Trapper''' will target it by laying its traps directly at the enemy. It takes it 0.5 seconds to throw a trap, with the thrown traps having a velocity of 15. The only exception is when it is set to ''Random''. Although a random enemy will still be highlighted when the '''Trapper''' is selected, the '''Trapper''' will lay its traps randomly and not at the highlighted enemy. There is a 10 second cooldown before a trap can be changed again. There are three types of traps that the '''Trapper''' can place down. The first is the spike trap, which is available from Level 0. Spike traps have a set amount of health, which when decreased to zero will make them disappear. This trap can hit as many enemies as long as it still has health. This trap can also deal more damage than its health, as the damage it deals is separate from its health. For example, if a spike trap has 1 health out of 60 left, an enemy that steps on it will receive the full 25 damage, if its health is at least 25. Spike traps get smaller as their health gets lower. The second type is the landmine, which is unlocked at Level 2. When an enemy steps on it, it will quickly explode, dealing splash damage to all enemies caught in its explosion and applying burn. The third and last trap is the bear trap, which is unlocked at Level 4. This trap, unlike the two previous traps, only deals damage to a single enemy. However, it deals higher damage than the other two traps and additionally stuns the enemy it hits for 3 seconds. Each trap has a lifespan before disappearing. This lifespan will reset once it is used, however, as all of them except spike trap disappear on a single hit, this has little use for most of the traps. The '''Trapper''' is considered an all-rounder tower as its cheap cost allows it to be used in the early game, while later on its upgraded traps deal immense damage to crowds and have great supporting utility. The '''Trapper''' has a placement limit of seven per player. ==Upgrades== {{PVPTabber |{{Upgrade|Level = Level 1|Upgrade Title = Sharper Spikes|Cost = {{Money|500}}|Image = [[Mission Quests|Mission Quest]] |[[Void Crate]] |[[Beach Crate]] |} ==Strategy== *As it takes a long time for the '''Trapper''' to place down its traps, it is generally recommended to place the tower in the back, where it has more time to pile up traps. **The [[Commander]] can also be used to decrease the '''Trapper's''' firerate, allowing it to place down more traps quicker. *The '''Trapper's''' spikes can be very useful early on at dealing with both hordes of weaker enemies such as the [[Abnormal]], though due to their low damage they are not effective against higher health enemies like the [[Normal Boss]] until later upgrades or when upgraded. **It is generally best to place down multiple Level 1 or 2 '''Trappers''' early on because of their cost efficiency. *Landmines can be quite useful at clearing out hordes of high health enemies, because of their high damage, them setting enemies on fire and their ability to ignore defense. *Bear traps only deal damage to a single enemy, meaning that it should generally only be used for high health enemies. **It is best to set the '''Trapper's''' targeting to ''Strongest'', as it means that the bear traps are less likely hit enemies with lower health. **Additionally, the bear traps stun enemies for three seconds, making them quite effective at stalling enemies. ***If an enemy has [[Stun Immunity]] or is a [[Boss]] enemy, it will not be stunned but only slowed down instead. *When the '''Trapper''' is set to ''Random'', it will not target a random enemy — it will instead drop its traps in random spots. *The '''Trapper's''' spike and bear trap damage is unaffected by [[Damage Buff]]s, so pairing these traps with [[Damage Buff]]ing towers like the [[DJ Booth]] or [[Mercenary Base]] is useless. *The '''Trapper''' is very useful on maps with longer paths, as it gives the tower more time to accumulate traps before enemies get to them. *While the '''Trapper''' itself does not have lead detection, its traps will still damage [[Lead (Attribute)|Lead]] enemies, making it effective against these types of enemies. **However, the '''Trapper''' is unable to directly throw traps at [[Flying]] enemies due to its aforementioned lack of flying detection. **While the traps can hit hidden and lead enemies, they cannot hit [[Flying]] enemies, as they will fly over it. **As the spike and bear traps deal damage like unit collision, they cannot hit [[Ghost (Attribute)|Ghost]] enemies. However, the landmine is not affected by this. *The '''Trapper's''' spike and bear traps are very useful against enemies with the tank attribute, as they deal damage to them at a quick speed. ==Trivia== *The '''Trapper''' is loosely based on the [[w:c:bloons:Spike_Factory (BTD6)|Spike Factory]] from the '''''Bloons Tower Defense''''' series. *Prior to the 11th of June 2025, the Level 3 '''Trapper''' with spike traps selected had the highest firerate of any tower in the game, that being 7.5 without the [[Firerate Bug]]. **The current tower with the highest firerate is the Level 4 [[Ranger]]. ==Update History== ''For previous cosmetic variations, see the [[/Gallery|gallery]] page.'' {{scroll|text = *'''24 February 2024''' - [[v1.14.0]] **'''Trapper''' added. **{{Bug}} Spike and bear traps deal incorrect amounts of damage to enemies with defense.
